questionsToConsider: What's the smallest and largest guest count you'll cater, and should the form say so?
Which service styles do you actually offer?
Do you need the venue address to price travel, and does an outdoor event change your equipment list?
Would a tasting session be part of your process for bigger events?
guide.howToUseResponses: Check the date and guest count first, since those decide whether you can take the job at all. Use the service style, kitchen answer and equipment list to work out staffing and what goes in the van. The ranking tells you how to pitch the proposal: someone who put budget first wants two clear price options, someone who put presentation first wants photos. Reply quickly, because people planning events often ask several caterers at once.
customizeSteps: Swap the food styles for the cuisines and menus you're known for.
Set the serving time window on the date question to the hours you work.
Link to the form from your menu page, or embed it on your website's catering page.

faqs.q: What should a catering inquiry form include?
faqs.a: The occasion, date and time, guest count, venue, service style, dietary needs and a budget. With those you can write a proposal without a long phone call first.

faqs.q: Why ask for budget per guest rather than a total?
faqs.a: Per guest is how most caterers price, and it's easier for a client to estimate. You can still multiply it by the guest count.

faqs.q: How do I handle allergies on a catering form?
faqs.a: Ask which needs apply, then confirm the exact numbers and severity when you follow up. The notes field is there for anything serious.

faqs.q: Can I skip questions that don't apply?
faqs.a: Yes. This template already skips the kitchen and equipment questions for drop-off orders, and you can edit or add branches to suit your service.
